subject: Day 72: peek-a-boo for laughs
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi's social reciprocity is sharpening into recognizable personality, and full laughs are emerging in the typical 10-to-14-week window. Today's lead is reciprocal laughter play.

Action items
- Play peek-a-boo in short rounds during an awake-alert window and watch for chuckles or full laughs; the back-and-forth surprise is the active ingredient. Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Start tracking sleep windows now: last wake time, time he fell asleep, and nap length. The pattern stabilizes by 12 to 14 weeks and gives you an anchor for a loose schedule.
- Continue the caregiver-vaccine and childcare-backup work from earlier this week if either is still open.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Hiccups after feeds and non-painful spit-up; spit-up volume should be trending down as the upper esophageal sphincter matures.
- [monitor] No social smile by now, or persistent head asymmetry suggesting positional plagiocephaly; raise repositioning or PT at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] Decreased feeding sustained over 24 hours, or new color changes during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, blue lips, or labored breathing. Call the pediatrician same-day, and call 911 for blue lips!

Enrichment opportunities
- Run peek-a-boo as social-cognition practice: the reciprocal turn-taking is what laughter rewards, and it builds the same exchange circuitry as conversation. Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Keep extending his cooing exchanges, leaving longer pauses so he takes more turns; vocal range is widening now. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Stack 60 to 75 minutes of tummy time across the day, looking for chest fully off the floor on his forearms. HealthyChildren tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 84-91 (~3 months): sleep-consolidation window opens; first laugh often consolidates around here too.
- Day 112-126 (4-month visit): RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
